Operator: Good morning, and welcome to the Aegis Insurance Group Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants will be in listen-only mode. After today's presentation, there will be an opportunity to ask questions. As a reminder, please limit yourself to one question and one follow-up. As a further reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the conference over to Emily Carter, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Emily Carter: Thank you, Operator, and good morning, everyone. Welcome to Aegis Insurance Group's Q3 2024 earnings call. Joining me on the call today are Johnathan Hale, Chief Executive Officer; Michael Reynolds, Chief Financial Officer; and Lisa Patel, Chief Underwriting Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that some of the statements we are making today may be considered forward-looking. These statements are subject to certain risks and uncertainties that could cause our actual results to differ materially from those projected. We encourage you to review our SEC filings for a more detailed discussion of these risks and uncertainties.

I will now turn the call over to Johnathan Hale.

Johnathan Hale: Thank you, Emily, and good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining us today. I'm pleased to report on Aegis Insurance Group's performance for Q3 2024. We delivered strong results, driven by robust new business production across our P&C and Life & Health segments, disciplined pricing actions that supported premium volume growth despite some policy count softness, solid GWP expansion by line of business in a hardening market, and an improved investment income yield benefiting from higher rates and strategic allocation. These factors combined to produce meaningful top-line momentum and bottom-line profitability while maintaining underwriting discipline.

Michael, our CFO, will now provide a more detailed review of our financial performance.

Michael Reynolds: Thank you, Johnathan. Good morning, everyone. As Johnathan mentioned, we had a solid quarter. Our net income was $450 million, or $1.85 per share. Key drivers of our financial performance included strong new business production, effective pricing adjustments offsetting volume sensitivities, broad-based GWP growth, and elevated investment returns. Our combined ratio was 92.5%, reflecting effective underwriting and claims management. We continue to maintain a strong capital position, with a 450% NAIC RBC ratio.

Let me now turn to our new business production volume, a key leading indicator of our top-line growth trajectory and market share expansion. For the quarter, we delivered robust results across both our Property & Casualty (P&C) and Life & Health segments, with total new business production reaching $2.8 billion in annualized premium equivalent (APE) – that's up 18% year-over-year and 7% sequentially from Q2. In terms of policy count, we wrote 1.45 million new policies, a 22% increase YoY, reflecting strong demand in both personal and commercial lines amid favorable rate environments and our accelerated digital distribution strategy.

Let me break this down by segment for clarity. Starting with P&C, which accounted for 62% of our new business mix at $1.74 billion in gross written premiums (GWP) for new policies – up 16% YoY. Personal lines drove the lion's share here, with auto new business GWP hitting $850 million, a standout 21% YoY increase. This was fueled by our 'Aegis DriveSafe' telematics program, now active with over 450,000 enrolled policyholders, mirroring successes seen at peers like Progressive and Root Insurance. Usage-based pricing has not only boosted conversion rates by 28% but also improved our underlying loss ratios by de-risking our book – early data shows a 15% reduction in claims frequency for high-engagement users.

Homeowners and renters new business added $420 million in GWP, up 12% YoY, despite persistent catastrophe pressures from Hurricane season. We gained 2.5 points of market share in the Southeast U.S., leveraging our partnerships with homebuilders like Lennar and D.R. Horton for embedded insurance at the point of sale – a channel now contributing 18% of our personal P&C new business, up from 8% a year ago. Commercial P&C rounded out the segment at $470 million, up 10% YoY, with strong uptake in small business owners' policies (BOP) and cyber add-ons, where we saw 35% growth amid rising ransomware threats. Our AI-powered underwriting engine, Aegis IntelliQuote, processed 75% of these submissions in under 5 minutes, driving a 19% improvement in bind rates versus manual processes.

Shifting to Life & Health, we generated $1.06 billion in present value of new business premiums (PVNBP), up an impressive 22% YoY – well ahead of the industry average of 12% as reported by LIMRA. Term life dominated with $520 million APE, up 25%, benefiting from our direct-to-consumer digital platform, which now captures 42% of applications – a channel mix shift accelerated by integrations with fintechs like Lemonade and Oscar Health. Universal life and indexed products contributed $310 million APE, up 18%, as affluent clients responded to our enhanced riders for long-term care and critical illness, positioning us competitively against Prudential and Lincoln Financial.

Whole life new business APE was $150 million, up 15%, with notable traction in our jumbo case pipeline targeting high-net-worth individuals via advisor networks. Health new business, including employer group and individual ACA plans, added $80 million APE, up 20%, driven by expansions into Medicare Advantage supplements in partnership with UnitedHealth Group – a strategic move to tap the $400 billion MA market amid CMS rate hikes.

Regionally, North America remains our powerhouse at 68% of total new business volume, up 17% YoY, with California and Florida leading due to rate adequacy post-wildfires and storms. Europe contributed 15%, with $420 million APE equivalent, up 25% on the back of our UK motor relaunch and German commercial growth, where we've clawed back 1.8 points of share from Aviva and Allianz through competitive pricing and our ESG-linked green building discounts. Asia-Pacific was the fastest grower at 12% of mix and 32% YoY expansion to $336 million, led by India life sales via our Bajaj Allianz JV and telematics auto in Australia, capitalizing on post-COVID protection gaps.

Strategically, these results underscore our 'Digital First, Customer Centric' initiative, including the rollout of our AegisOne app – now with 2.2 million MAUs – which embedded 25% of Q3 new business through API partnerships with banks like JPMorgan Chase and auto dealers. We've also invested in predictive analytics using alternative data sources like credit bureau insights and satellite imagery for P&C risk selection, yielding a 14% uplift in new business profitability margins, with value of new business (VNB) margins expanding 220 basis points to 28%.

Looking forward, we expect Q4 new business production to accelerate to 20%+ YoY growth, supported by rate momentum – industry-wide P&C rate increases averaged 9.2% per latest Carrier Management data – and our $250 million tech spend on GenAI for personalized quoting. This positions us to outpace peers like Travelers and Chubb in market share while maintaining combined ratios below 95%.

Turning now to the impact of our pricing discipline on premium volume, total net written premiums grew 6.2% year-over-year to $11.4 billion in Q3, marking our ninth consecutive quarter of organic premium growth. This was driven predominantly by targeted pricing actions averaging 9.8% across our in-force book, which more than offset a modest 3.1% contraction in policy count. To put this in context, our premium elasticity – the sensitivity of volume to rate changes – has stabilized at around -0.35, meaning for every 1% rate increase, we see roughly a 0.35% decline in volume. This is a marked improvement from the -0.6 elasticity we experienced in 2022 during the height of the 'rate shock' cycle, when softer competitors like Geico and Progressive aggressively chased market share.

Diving deeper by segment: Personal Auto, which is 42% of premiums, saw us implement average rate increases of 11.2% on renewals, up from 9.5% in Q2, to address ballooning loss costs from repair inflation (now +15% YoY per Mitchell data) and higher claim frequency tied to distracted driving trends. This propelled auto written premiums up 7.8% to $4.8 billion. Policy count dipped 2.7% due to some price-sensitive shoppers migrating to direct writers, but our retention held steady at 87.2% – bolstered by our Snapshot telematics program, which now covers 28% of our book and delivers 15-20% better loss ratios for safe drivers. New business grew 1.2%, supported by targeted digital marketing in growth markets.

Next, on Gross Written Premiums, or GWP, which grew 12.4% year-over-year to $8.7 billion in the quarter. This marks our strongest quarterly GWP growth since Q4 2021, driven by a combination of disciplined rate increases, improved retention, and robust new business wins across our diversified book. Excluding the impact of foreign exchange headwinds in Europe, where the euro depreciated 5% against the USD, our underlying GWP growth was an even healthier 14.1%.

Let me break this down by line of business, underscoring our strategic execution in a hardening market. Personal Lines – 37% of total GWP – delivered 15.2% GWP growth to $3.2 billion. Personal Auto grew 17.8%, fueled by average rate increases of 9.2% amid persistent inflationary pressures on repair costs, including OEM parts shortages and skilled labor premiums echoing supply chain disruptions post-COVID. We also expanded our telematics penetration to 28% of policies via our AegisDrive app, partnering with tech leaders like Cambridge Mobile Telematics, which improved risk selection and boosted new business by 22%. Homeowners & Dwelling grew 12.5%, benefiting from 7.8% rate hikes in high-exposure states like Florida and California, where wildland-urban interface risks are intensifying due to climate change. Retention here held steady at 89%, above our 87% target, thanks to our AI-powered pricing engine that dynamically adjusts for loss trends.

Commercial P&C – 36% of the mix – saw 11.7% GWP growth to $3.1 billion. Commercial Property & Casualty surged 14.3%, capturing share in middle-market segments with 8.5% rate adequacy gains, particularly in excess & surplus lines where capacity constraints from carriers like Chubb and Travelers created tailwinds. We wrote $450 million in new E&S business, up 25%, leveraging our delegated authority partnerships with MGAs like Ryan Specialty Group. Workers' Compensation grew a more modest 6.2%, pressured by medical inflation trending at 5.9% – in line with NCCI estimates – but offset by 11% premium growth in our high-deductible group captives, which now comprise 15% of the book. Overall retention improved to 91%, reflecting our focus on account-based underwriting with predictive analytics from tools like Verisk's ISO rating platform.

Specialty & Liability – 16% of GWP – grew 9.8% to $1.4 billion. Cyber Insurance jumped 22.4% to $520 million, driven by 12% rates and expanded limits in response to the MOVEit breach fallout and surging ransomware claims – our loss ratio here remains disciplined at 62%, below peers. Directors & Officers grew 10.1%, benefiting from public company IPO activity and M&A tailwinds, while our Marine and Energy book expanded 8.7% in the Gulf Coast region, hedging against offshore wind delays. We strategically ceded 25% of this growth to our quota-share treaty with Berkshire Hathaway, maintaining combined ratio discipline.

Life & Health – 11% of the mix – grew 8.3% to $1.0 billion through group life renewals and supplemental health products. This was tempered by competitive pressures in individual life, but our accident & health wrappers around P&C policies added $120 million in cross-sell premiums.

Geographically, North America drove 68% of growth at 14.8%, with California and Texas propelling personal lines amid rate filings approved by state regulators. EMEA grew 7.2% on a constant FX basis, led by UK motor with 11% rates post-Flood Re expansions, though German flood losses from Storm Hans capped momentum. Asia-Pacific accelerated 18.5%, with Hong Kong commercial lines up 25% on China reopening and our JV with Ping An Insurance enhancing distribution.

This GWP trajectory reflects our 'Precision Growth' strategy: layering advanced telematics and machine learning underwriting – powered by our in-house AegisAI platform, which reduced adverse selection by 15% – onto a foundation of rate discipline. We've invested $150 million this year for digital brokers and embedded insurance APIs, akin to Lemonade's model but scaled for enterprises, targeting 20% new business from partnerships like Allianz Trade. Looking forward, we expect full-year GWP growth of 11-13%, with Q4 acceleration from seasonal auto renewals and catastrophe reinsurance renewals at favorable terms. Our 1-in-250 year tower remains intact, and while risks include secondary perils like California wildfires, our attritional loss ratio of 58% positions us well versus the industry's 62% per AM Best.

Finally, I'd like to spend some time on our investment income yield, a cornerstone of our earnings power. For those less familiar, investment income yield represents the annualized return on our invested assets, calculated as net investment income divided by the average invested assets over the period. We report both our book yield – which is more GAAP-oriented and includes some amortization effects – and our portfolio yield, which gives a cleaner view excluding certain non-cash items like OTTI charges or premium amortization.

Our core portfolio yield came in at 4.2% for Q3, up 40 basis points quarter-over-quarter and a robust 85 basis points year-over-year from 3.35% in Q3 2023. On a trailing 12-month basis, this expanded to 4.15%, marking our strongest full-year yield since the pre-pandemic era. This performance drove $1.2 billion in net investment income for the quarter, a 12% increase YoY, comfortably covering our cost of liabilities even as claims inflation ticked up to 5.2% in P&C lines.

Breaking this down by key drivers: Our $180 billion general account portfolio remains conservatively positioned, with 72% in fixed income – split roughly 40% investment-grade corporates, 15% municipals, 10% U.S. Treasuries and agencies, and 7% structured credits like CMBS and ABS. Equities are at a disciplined 12%, focused on high-quality dividend payers like those in the S&P 500 Financials and Utilities sectors, yielding about 3.8% on average. Alternatives round out at 16%, including core REITs, infrastructure funds, and a modest allocation to private credit via evergreen funds – these delivered a standout 6.1% yield, helping offset any public market volatility.

The big tailwind has been the higher-for-longer rate environment. Post-Fed hikes, our new money yield – on the $15 billion we reinvested in Q3 – hit 5.1%, well above our benchmark Barclays Intermediate Aggregate Index at 4.6%. We're actively extending duration slightly to 5.8 years from 5.4 a year ago, locking in these levels while maintaining strong ALM matching to our liabilities. Our liability duration sits at 6.2 years, predominantly from long-tail life and annuity products, so this positioning shields us from reinvestment risk as the yield curve uninverts.

Regionally, performance varied thoughtfully. In the U.S., which comprises 65% of our portfolio, yields benefited from a steepening Treasury curve – our muni book yielded 3.9% tax-equivalent, enhanced by AMT-exempt issues from blue-chip issuers like California GO bonds. Europe, at 20% of AUM, saw yields rise to 3.7% on Eurozone sovereigns and covered bonds, though ECB rate cuts pressured shorter-end peripherals; we've tilted toward German Pfandbriefe for stability. Asia-Pacific, our growth engine at 15%, delivered 4.8% via JGBs and AUD corporates, with strategic overweight to Singapore dollar floating-rate notes amid RBA hawkishness. Currency hedges via FX forwards kept FX drag minimal at just 2 bps.

On the technical front, we've rolled out several initiatives to enhance yields without compromising our AA- rating or 450% NAIC RBC. Our dynamic ALM platform, powered by BlackRock's Aladdin, now optimizes cash flows daily across 50,000+ positions, capturing an extra 15 bps in yield through opportunistic buys like BBB investment-grade credits during August's market dip. We've ramped ESG integration – 28% of new fixed income is SFDR Article 8/9 compliant, including green bonds from issuers like Enel and Ørsted, yielding competitively at 4.4% while appealing to our annuity clientele. We're dipping into private assets more aggressively: a $2 billion commitment to Ares and Apollo evergreen credit funds targets 7-8% net yields, with first closings already contributing 22 bps to Q3 results. And on derivatives, our $10 billion interest rate swap book – receiving fixed at 4.0% – buffered against the front-end drop, preserving 10 bps of spread.

Strategically, this isn't just about chasing yield; it's about de-risking for the long haul. With group annuities growing 18% YoY to $45 billion in reserves, we're prioritizing spread compression avoidance – our investment spread over new money cost held steady at 110 bps. Compared to peers like Prudential or Athene, our 4.2% yield outperforms their 3.9% average, thanks to lower legacy low-yield books; we've amortized down sub-3% holdings to under 8% of the portfolio. Looking ahead, we guide to 4.3-4.5% portfolio yield in 2025, assuming no recession, with upside from potential Fed pauses and our $5 billion annual alternative pipeline.

Of course, risks remain: credit spreads widened 15 bps in Q3 on office CMBS exposure (just 1.2% of portfolio, all performing), and equity volatility from geopolitical tensions could pressure our 12% allocation. But with $4.5 billion in liquidity and a 1.5x coverage ratio, we're well-fortified.

In summary, our investment income yield underscores Aegis's disciplined, high-conviction approach – turning the float into a profit engine amid normalizing rates.

Operator, we are now ready to open the line for questions.

Operator: Thank you. The floor has been opened for questions. [Operator Instructions] Our first question comes from David Wong with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

David Wong: Good morning, team. Can you provide more color on the new business profitability margins and how the VNB expansion ties into your Q4 outlook?

Johnathan Hale: Good morning, David. Thanks for the question. As Michael outlined, our VNB margins expanded 220 basis points to 28%, driven by the 14% uplift from predictive analytics and alternative data in risk selection. This profitability is embedded in our book, with telematics and AI underwriting ensuring we only take on attractive risks. For Q4, with 20%+ new business growth expected on 9.2% industry rate momentum and GenAI quoting, we see sustained margin expansion, supporting combined ratios below 95% even as cat activity persists. Lisa, any underwriting color?

Lisa Patel: Absolutely, Johnathan. Our focus on de-risking via Aegis IntelliQuote and DriveSafe has lowered claims frequency, directly boosting VNB. We're confident in the trajectory.

Operator: Our next question comes from Sarah Kim with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

Sarah Kim: Good morning. Could you discuss the impact of recent catastrophe events like Hurricane season on your pricing and GWP growth outlook?

Michael Reynolds: Good morning, Sarah. Despite pressures from Hurricane season and events like Idalia or Maui-like wildfires, our pricing discipline – averaging 9.8% increases – and reinsurance tower have kept us resilient. GWP grew 12.4% organically, with personal lines at 15.2% even in high-exposure areas through rate hikes and telematics. Retention at 89% in homeowners shows price elasticity working in our favor. For outlook, we expect 11-13% full-year growth, with Q4 boosted by renewals and favorable re-tower terms.

Operator: Our next question comes from Robert Ellis with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

Robert Ellis: Thanks. On investment yield, how are you thinking about private credit allocation amid spread widening?

Michael Reynolds: Robert, great question. Our 16% alts bucket, including private credit via Ares and Apollo, yielded 6.1% and added 22 bps this quarter. We're committing $2 billion more to evergreen funds targeting 7-8% net, balanced against our conservative fixed income core. Spread widening offers entry points, but we cap at risk limits to protect the AA- rating – liquidity at $4.5 billion gives flexibility.

Operator: There are no further questions at this time.

Johnathan Hale: Thank you for your questions and your interest in Aegis Insurance Group. In closing, we are confident in our ability to continue delivering strong results and creating value for our shareholders, powered by digital innovation, pricing discipline, and prudent capital management. Thank you for joining us today.

Operator: This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
